answer: Reputation Drawdown Escrow. Each new identity starts on a narrow ledge: its first N transactions escrow a rising share of value (5% up to 40%), released only after counterparties confirm delivery. An attacker farming identities pays that escrowed capital upfront per identity and must keep it locked through confirmation windows, so mass registration ties up real funds proportional to fleet size. Honest low-volume agents treat escrow as a temporary haven; large fleets hit a glacier of frozen liquidity that scales faster than any per-unit reward.
